alt: Supervised learning: the model learns from labeled data, a mapping from input X to output Y. Example: cat versus dog images with labels go through a deep neural network to a predicted label. Applications: image, speech and text classification, object detection, medical diagnosis, sentiment analysis.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Unsupervised learning: the model learns from unlabeled data and discovers hidden patterns or structure. Example: customer segmentation shown as three clusters on a feature 1 versus feature 2 plot. Applications: clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Reinforcement learning: an agent sends an action to the environment and gets back a reward and the new state. Steps: observe state, take action, receive reward, update policy. Goal: maximize cumulative reward. Applications: game playing, robotics, autonomous driving.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut

alt: Table of four types, supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement and hybrid, with what each learns from, whether it needs labels, its main goal and examples.
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Deep network architectures split into unsupervised (autoencoders, deep belief networks, GANs), supervised (CNN, RNN, LSTM) and hybrid (a combination of unsupervised and supervised methods).
author: Deep Learning faculty

alt: Basic terminologies of deep learning with a short explanation of each: neuron (node), layer, dataset, weight (parameters), bias, activation function, loss function (cost function), optimizer, learning rate and epoch.
author: Prof. Karishma Raut
